titulo: Strategies for understanding and being understood: False friends

aula.titulo: Strategies for understanding and being understood
aula.objetivo: Understand more than you know (similar words, word families, false friends), work around missing words and ask for help without stalling the conversation.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «rester» = to stay: «Je reste à Paris.» (not «to rest») STEP 2: «demander» = to ask (not “to demand”): «Il demande un café.» «Elle demande l'heure.» STEP 3: «attendre» = to wait (not “to attend”): «J'attends le bus.» STEP 4: «exprès» = on purpose (not “express”): «Il l'a fait exprès.» STEP 5: «sale» = dirty (not “sale”): «Mes mains sont sales.» STEP 6: «ignorer» = not to know (not “to ignore”): «J'ignore la réponse.» STEP 7: «magasin» = shop (not «magazine»): «Il y a un magasin près d'ici.» STEP 8: «blesser» = to hurt, to wound (not “to bless”): «Il s'est blessé à la jambe.» STEP 9: «tirer» = to pull (not “to tire”): «Tirez la porte.»
blocos.comparacao: in English, «to wait» and «to attend» are the ones that confuse most: French «attendre» means to wait, not to attend. And «ignorer» is not to deliberately overlook, but to not know: «j'ignore» = «I don't know».

erros.errado: J'attends le client. (in place of «I serve»)
erros.certo: Je reçois le client. / Je sers le client.

erros.errado: Je demande si tu as faim. (in place of «I demand»)
erros.certo: Je te demande si tu as faim.
erros.motivo: «Demander» means to ask, never to demand.

blocos.enunciado: Say aloud six sentences, one with each false friend: rester, demander, attendre, exprès, sale, ignorer.
Give one example of each shortcut: cognate, word family, prefix.
